newsitem.title: USA: Birmingham Steel Louisiana venture funded.
newsitem.headline: Birmingham Steel Louisiana venture funded.

text.p: Birmingham Steel Corp said Tuesday financing arrangements for construction of a direct reduced iron venture in Louisiana have been completed.

Financing was arranged through American Iron Reduction, LLC, the 50/50 venture the company formed with GS Industries to construct and operate the facility, which will produce some 1.2 million metric tons per year of DRI for sale to the steelmaking units of the venture partners.
The $200 million funding package was concluded on a project finance basis, providing non-recourse, off-balance- sheet treatment for both partners, Birmingham Steel said.
to The fully underwritten financing was led by NationsBank Capital Markets and co-led by CIBC Wood Gundy.
The American Iron facility is being constructed by Bechtel Corp on a site near Convent, in St. James Parish, La. It is expected to be completed by calendar year-end 1997.

The site on which the plant is being built has been developed in cooperation with the Illinois Central Railroad. The Illinois Central Corp operating unit is also developing a bulk commodities handling terminal adjacent to the site which will provide material handling services to American Iron.

Birmingham Steel said it and GS Industries continue to pursue plans to construct a second Midrex DRI unit of equal capacity on the current site. The partners are in talks with other companies that are interested in purchasing DRI produced by a second unit, the company explained.

It said the site infrastructure is designed to accommodate the second unit and the required permitting for the second unit already has been obtained. The second unit expansion may be brought on-stream as early as mid-1998.
